headline: Brazil to implement 'sin tax' on tobacco and beverages in 2027
summary: Brazil will begin applying a new 'sin tax' on products including cigarettes, spirits, and sugary drinks starting in February 2027. Tax rates will vary by product, reaching up to 66.7%.
why: New excise taxes impact the margins of consumer goods companies and can influence consumer demand patterns for the affected categories.

impacts.name: Consumer Staples
impacts.why: Higher excise taxes typically reduce profit margins or force price increases that dampen demand.
